note: modern = 10 bodies (app set), 1700–2200 CE daily, Pluto-valid range. deep = 7 classical bodies, 20000 BCE–2200 CE 3-day step (the 7-classical set is fast and its mean motion is secularly stable, so conjunction dates stay trustworthy across the whole range; beyond ~±4000 y from J2000 the VSOP87/ELP perturbation terms diverge, so exact degrees — and thus the sign of a given deep-past conjunction — are an extrapolation). maxInSign = count in the most-occupied single sign; span = smallest arc (°) containing all bodies; era = precessional era (~2147 y each, cyclic mod the ~25771-y great year). Per-event stellar readings are computed in the browser for the selected alignment (skyAt is fast); the cross-check summary is stored here.

crossCheck.verdict: NO unique 7-classical reading arises on rare alignments. Concentrating planets in one zodiacal sign REDUCES reading richness: Genesis-legibility 0.0% (rare) vs 0.1% (baseline), avg readable names 826 vs 1486, and the SAME 13 Shem HaMephorash angel-roots (0 new). Clustering lowers letter diversity — rare alignments are a rarity filter, not a richness source.
